overview: This file concerns alleged violations of Japanese fortified-zone airspace around Dairen in the Kwantung Leased Territory during 1931. It combines cross-reference sheets with a consular despatch on a British commercial aircraft that became lost in a blizzard and landed at Dairen, where its pilot was summarily fined, and correspondence about three hydroplanes from the U.S. aircraft tender JASON whose navigation flight prompted Japan to request an expression of regret. Collectively, the documents illuminate Japanese airspace restrictions, summary judicial procedure, consular intervention, and the diplomatic handling of accidental flights near sensitive military installations.

people.name: William Cameron Forbes
people.role: American diplomatic representative in Japan, described in the note as the American Minister at Tokyo

people.name: Nelson Trusler Johnson
people.role: American Minister to China at Peiping

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Forbes despatch on flights over fortified zones
subfiles.about: The sheet directs researchers to Despatch No. 103 concerning requirements for aircraft flying over fortified zones in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: This filing note cross-references document 894.7961/7, a despatch from Forbes in Japan dated January 12, 1931. The referenced despatch records the American representative's comments on requirements governing airplane flights over fortified areas of the Kwantung Leased Territory.

subfiles.title: British airplane violation of the Kwantung fortified zone
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Coville reports the disposition of a case involving a British commercial aircraft that accidentally entered the Kwantung Leased Territory and landed at Dairen.
subfiles.summary: A Far East Aviation Company airplane traveling from Mukden to Tientsin became disoriented in a blizzard, followed the wrong railway, and landed at Dairen on February 9, 1931. Despite the Acting British Consul's apology and insistence that the incursion was accidental, the civilian pilot was convicted through summary-court procedure and fined 200 yen or forty days' hard labor without being present or represented. No appeal was taken because of the likely delay, and the two airmen sailed with their aircraft for Shanghai; the matter was then referred to the British Embassy in Tokyo for negotiation with the Japanese Foreign Office.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Franklin despatch on American planes near Dairen
subfiles.about: The sheet directs researchers to another file containing Franklin's despatch about American aircraft appearing over a Japanese fortified zone near Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The filing note cross-references 811.30-Asiatic Fleet/85. It identifies a despatch from Chefoo concerning the Japanese government's desire that the American Consul at Dairen express regret for the appearance of American planes over the fortified zone.

subfiles.title: Despatch forwarding Japan's request for an expression of regret
subfiles.from: Lynn W. Franklin, American Consul at Chefoo
subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, American Minister at Peiping
subfiles.about: Franklin forwards his letter to the American Consul at Dairen concerning Japan's request for regrets over flights near Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Franklin encloses a letter reporting that the Japanese government wanted the American Consul at Dairen to express regret for the appearance of aircraft from the U.S. aircraft tender JASON over a fortified zone. He also refers Johnson to an earlier despatch of May 18 concerning naval aircraft operations at Chefoo. Copies were distributed to the Department of State and the commander in chief of the U.S. Asiatic Fleet at Qingdao.

subfiles.title: Letter on the JASON hydroplanes' navigation flight
subfiles.from: Lynn W. Franklin, American Consul at Chefoo
subfiles.to: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Franklin explains the flight path of three JASON hydroplanes and conveys Japan's request for an expression of regret to the Kwantung governor-general.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Consul at Chefoo requested that Langdon express regret on behalf of the JASON's captain to the governor-general at Port Arthur for three aircraft reportedly appearing over a fortified zone near Dairen on July 14. Franklin's investigation found that the hydroplanes had conducted a navigation flight near Round Island and Encounter Rock and that their navigators were unaware of entering Japanese territory or a fortified zone. He considered this account accurate and reported that the JASON's commander had ordered future flights to avoid the vicinity, while noting that no objections to earlier flights had been received.

interest: The file offers a compact comparison of British civilian and American naval encounters with Japan's protected airspace in the Kwantung Leased Territory. Particularly useful are the details of the British pilot's conviction without his presence or representation and the precise route and coordinates reported for the JASON hydroplanes. The cross-references also reveal how related diplomatic, aviation, and Asiatic Fleet records were dispersed across the State Department's decimal filing system.
